headline: Park Entry and Coastal Camping Reservations
reservation: A valid park pass is required for entry to all areas within the national park boundaries. While daily entry permits are typically available at gatehouse stations or visitor centers, overnight campsites and backcountry facilities require separate, advance reservations through the Parks Canada system. Systems for high-demand summer months often open in early spring, so check the official portal for current seasonal launch dates.

days.title: Inland Forests and Boreal Vistas

stops.name: Blue Hill Viewpoint
stops.detail: Drive or hike to the highest point in the park for a panoramic view of the rugged coastline and the intricate network of islands in Bonavista Bay.

stops.name: Ochre Hill
stops.detail: Ascend the fire tower trail to see how the boreal forest transitions into the rocky barrens characteristic of eastern Newfoundland.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transitions; conditions vary with wildlife crossings.
days.note: Moose are frequently active near the Trans-Canada Highway; remain vigilant during dawn and dusk travel.

days.title: Coastal Headlands and Saline Trails

stops.name: Coastal Trail
stops.detail: Walk the shoreline of the inner Newman Sound to observe the transition between tidal flats and dense forest growth.

stops.name: Pissing Mare Falls
stops.detail: Access this dramatic waterfall via the Western Brook Pond area to view one of the most photographed natural features in the region.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for park road navigation; conditions vary.
days.note: Tidal zones can be slippery; check local tide charts if exploring the intertidal areas near the sound.

days.title: Heritage Harbours and Sea Kayaking

stops.name: Sandy Cove Beach
stops.detail: Visit this rare sandy stretch for a swim in the sheltered waters of the North Atlantic.

stops.name: Salton's Brook
stops.detail: Explore the visitor center exhibits and depart from the wharf for guided water-based excursions into the narrow reaches of the park.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes between visitor hubs; conditions vary.
days.note: Water temperatures remain brisk even in peak summer; prepare for sudden coastal fog rolling in from the bay.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at popular spots like Blue Hill and Newman Sound may reach capacity during July weekends. Consider visiting secondary trailheads if main lots appear congested.

intel.title: Corridor Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable along the Trans-Canada Highway corridor but fades quickly in backcountry valleys. Download offline maps before departing from Gander or Clarenville.

intel.title: Gateway Service
intel.text: Fuel services are located in Glovertown and Clarenville, but there are no service stations within the park boundaries. Ensure tanks are sufficient for inland forest exploration.

intel.title: Seasonal Operation
intel.text: Full visitor services and washrooms typically operate from June through September. Outside this window, some secondary roads may be gated or unmaintained.

intel.title: Highway Safety
intel.text: The park is bisected by a major provincial highway used by heavy commercial traffic. Use designated pull-outs for sightseeing rather than stopping on the highway shoulder.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Gander International Airport (YQX), stock up on groceries in Gander, and drive south to the Glovertown park entrance.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are suitable for paved park roads; high-clearance vehicles are not required for main sights.
plan.goldenHour: Ochre Hill Lookout provides an expansive western view for sunset, though visibility is highly dependent on Atlantic fog patterns.
